evidence.summary: Exhaustive sweep of all 63488 finite FP16 encodings: 7 inputs produce FP16 outputs that differ (1 ulp) from the FP64-correctly-rounded sigmoid. All mismatches are near-zero inputs where the true sigmoid sits within ~1e-9 of an FP16 rounding boundary; FP32 intermediate error (~1e-7) flips the final cvt.rn. Example: x=0.0029296875, exact sigmoid=0.50073242135 < midpoint 0.500732421875, so correct RNE output is 0.50048828125, but kernel outputs 0.5009765625.

rationale: Internal FP32 exp and division each carry up to ~0.5-1 ulp FP32 error; on inputs where the true sigmoid sits exactly at an FP16 rounding boundary (tie or near-tie), FP32-level error can flip the final cvt.rn rounding, violating the round-once requirement.

scope_evidence.summary: Each output must be the sigmoid value rounded ONCE to binary16 RNE; 'One failing legal input is evidence against the implementation'; every finite FP16 encoding is legal.

scope_rationale: Contract requires exact bit-exact FP16 outputs equal to correctly-rounded sigmoid for every finite FP16 input; a single mismatched legal input is a violation.
statement: The kernel's FP32 intermediate arithmetic causes at least one legal finite FP16 input to produce a bit pattern differing from the FP64-correctly-rounded sigmoid.
